stem: Tejas hears the claim: "A larger whole number always has more prime factors, counting multiplicity, than a smaller whole number." He checks $81 = 3^{4}$ and $64 = 2^{6}$.

parts.text: Does one verified counterexample overturn the claim?

options.text: The answer is the word counterexample.
Yes: $81$ is larger than $64$ but has fewer prime factors counting multiplicity ($4$ against $6$), so the universal claim fails.
The claim still holds because some larger numbers do have more prime factors.
The claim is true because $81$ is the larger printed number.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A single explicit counterexample overturns a universal claim; $81=3^{4}$ has four prime factors and $64=2^{6}$ has six, so a larger number can have fewer factors.

teacher.key_rationale: 81>64 but 3^4 has four prime factors while 2^6 has six, so one counterexample disproves the universal claim. Naming the word alone, keeping the claim because other cases fit, or grabbing the larger print all miss that logic.
